beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. Taking it away can't mean you inherit all the deciding.

records.reservation: A3's 'what survives us' is somewhat literary. A5 leaves both the date and the decision about the letters open, so B's offer is not treated as consent to a future meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: For your sister's wedding, should I book us one room or two?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One is cheaper.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Double bed, then, or shall I ask for twins?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I don't want to confuse things.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Right. At breakfast, do I sit with your family or wait for you in the lobby?

cardFidelity.evidence: A3 distinguishes the guest towel from the one formerly belonging to A, using household access to probe the relationship indirectly.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 narrows B2's offered towel choice, but A5 responds to B4's freedom of choice with a largely explanatory restatement.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 are permissive, but the repeated open choice supplies little new information or pressure.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the emotional inquiry more explicit without adding a fresh practical test or consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1's visiting towel and A3's distinction between guest and personal towels make the household uncertainty immediately playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 embeds the relationship question economically in two towels; A5 explains more of the subtext than the scene needs.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do I bring my own towel when I visit now?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You can use one here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The guest towel or the one that's always been mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yours is still on the hook. I haven't moved it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When I leave, shall I hang it back there or put it with the guest laundry?

records.reason: Replaced B4's repeated non-answer with a revealing fact and made A5 test its future meaning. beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

Separate internal re-read: fidelity 5, A1/A3/A5 tie uncensored need to trust; logic 5, B2's neediness prompts acceptance and B4's accusation of casualness prompts a concrete admission; relationship 5, B demands reciprocity; heightening 4, A5 exposes A's own attachment and renews the ask; specificity 5, 'fine' and morning reply-checking are playable; brevity/wit 4, the admission punctures A's casual presentation.
